asks.tier.declarations: by declarations only; no intake agent ran
asks.compose.title: Ask the workspace
asks.compose.meta: kept by the service until it becomes quests
asks.compose.nowhere.headline: There is no workspace to ask yet
asks.compose.nowhere.body: An ask is made in a workspace, and a workspace exists once a repository is registered in it. Repositories says how one joins.
asks.compose.hint: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. The workspace's declarations propose where it belongs, and nothing is published until you name a receiver or accept a proposal.
asks.compose.hintIntake: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. This machine's intake agent reads it and publishes it where it belongs, and asks you when it cannot tell. Naming a receiver publishes it at once.
asks.compose.hintUnknown: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. Naming a receiver publishes it at once. Otherwise the workspace's declarations propose where it belongs, or the machine's intake agent, where one is set, reads it and publishes.
asks.compose.toNobody: Nobody yet — let the declarations propose
asks.compose.reviewOn: Review it in the default environment
asks.compose.reviewWords: why, if you want to say
asks.compose.reviewTwin: At a terminal, `daoris-driver ask --review rule|on|<environment>|off "…"` asks with the same choice, and `--review-words "…"` says why.
asks.record.reviewByRule: Nothing chosen here: each repository's rule decides whether its work is reviewed.
asks.record.reviewTwin: At a terminal, `daoris-driver ask --set-review {{id}} on|<environment>|off "…"` sets the same choice, or applies a proposal.
asks.compose.filesLabel: files — kept on this machine until the ask becomes quests, then carried by each
asks.record.noProposal: No repository's declarations share its words. Name the receiver below.
asks.record.fileKept: kept on this machine until it becomes quests
asks.record.deleteConfirm: This removes the ask from this machine, and every quest it became goes with it. It cannot be undone.
asks.tier.intake: an intake session read it and published it
asks.record.tierIntakeUnpublished: by declarations; an intake read it and has not published
asks.gone.headline: This ask is no longer here
asks.gone.body: It was deleted, or it belongs to a workspace this window is not showing. Choose another in the list.
asks.record.closeLeaves: Closing leaves its quests as they are; Abandon declines them.
asks.record.pausedTip: Nothing of its work starts on this machine until you resume it.
asks.record.noDriver: Pausing and abandoning are a machine's driver's, so a browser offers neither: on the desktop, or at a terminal, `daoris-driver ask --pause {{id}}` and `daoris-driver ask --abandon {{id}}`.
asks.work.lead: Its work as this machine's driver reads it, which is what a pause or an abandon reaches.
asks.work.waits: Waits on the answer to its question below, and carries on by itself in the same tree once it comes.
asks.work.pausedHere: Paused with this ask, until you resume it.
asks.work.pausedOwn: Paused on its own: its own page resumes it, and resuming this ask does not.
asks.work.pausedAsk: Paused with ask #{{id}}, until that ask is resumed.
asks.work.pausedQuest: Paused with quest #{{id}}, until that quest is resumed.
asks.work.elsewhere: Taken on {{machine}}: a pause here does not reach it.
asks.work.elsewhereUnnamed: Taken on another machine: a pause here does not reach it.
asks.work.outside: Taken here outside Daoris: a pause does not reach it.
asks.goAhead.lead: Its sessions asked you for these, each once. Every session on the ask is handed your answer at its next start.
asks.goAhead.near: its words could not be told from #{{near}}'s, so it was asked again
